chunks: And Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from al-Hajjaj, from Safwan, from Musa, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

key_terms.أَحْمَدُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, a prominent narrator
key_terms.زُرَارَةُ: Zurarah ibn A'yan, a companion of the Imams
key_terms.مُوسَى: Musa ibn Abi al-Khattab, a narrator

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on dowry and wages in Shia jurisprudence according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him), transmitted through the reliable chain of al-Hajjaj and Safwan, reaffirms the legal principles concerning dowry (mahr) and wages within the context of marriage validity. It underscores the continuity of juristic reasoning in Shia fiqh, linking the specific conditions of financial obligations to the broader framework of marital contracts as detailed in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*.
